meta.title: Shtil VPN — sing-box client for Android, TV, Windows and macOS
meta.description: A VPN app on the sing-box core (VLESS + Reality) for Android phones, Android TV, Windows and macOS. Russian sites keep the direct route, the key comes from a Telegram bot, updates arrive over the air.

hero.lead: The app opens an encrypted tunnel to our server, while banks, government services and marketplaces keep loading directly — they stay fast and still see you from Russia.

download.ios: Open the bot — key for iPhone

split.lead: An ordinary VPN pushes every packet through the tunnel — and the bank starts treating you as a foreign visitor. Here the route forks on the device itself.
list: The lists of Russian domains and address ranges live inside the app and are never downloaded: a remote rule-set server can be unreachable from Russia, and then the VPN would refuse to start at all.
For domains on the direct route only IPv4 answers are returned — otherwise the device would follow an AAAA record past the route and the site still would not open.
Per-app routing: send only the apps you choose through the tunnel and leave the rest as they were.
Nothing is fetched at runtime: you switch it on and it works, even when third-party addresses are down.

schema.alt: Diagram: part of the traffic goes through our server, Russian sites go directly

captions: Phone: connected, server and traffic in view
TV: the same app, built for a remote

steps.lead: From download to a working connection is a few minutes, and no sign-up is involved.

items.title: Install the app
items.text: The file comes from here; Google Play and the App Store are not needed. Each system asks once — what exactly it says is written below.

items.title: Try it, or add a key
items.text: The app has a “Try now” button — two hours with no Telegram and no email. A permanent key comes from the bot as a link or a short code, and a TV reads that code from your phone screen.

items.title: Press “Connect”
items.text: One key works on the phone, the TV and the computer at once. When the key changes on the server, every device picks up the new one by itself.

price.lead: The bot issues and renews the subscription, and it also takes the payment — we collect nothing on this page.

items.note: Free, once per account. Plus two hours as a guest — no Telegram, straight from the app.
With a Russian bank card, through YooMoney.
Telegram Stars — for people without a Russian card. That is roughly 6 US dollars; we have no dollar checkout, the stars are bought inside Telegram.

install.h2: What the system says during installation
install.lead: The apps are distributed outside the stores, so each system asks once. That is how it greets any program that did not come from its own store.

items.text: “Installing from this source is not allowed” — let the browser install apps. Google may then show a red screen; the button you need there says “Install anyway”.
The same red Google screen; the confirm button sits at the bottom and is reached with the remote. Type the short address into a downloader app and the file starts right away.
A blue “Windows protected your PC” box → “More info” → “Run anyway”. We did not buy a publisher certificate: since 2024 instant trust is not for sale, reputation is earned through install count.
The first launch is refused: System Settings → Privacy & Security → “Open Anyway” and the administrator password. After that the app opens with a double click.

items.title: The sing-box core
items.text: VLESS + Reality over TCP. The core is open source and ships inside the app — no internet is needed for the first launch.

items.title: A subscription link, not a long key
items.text: The configuration arrives ready and refreshes itself. When the key changes on the server, nothing has to be mailed out to people.

items.title: Over-the-air updates
items.text: The app finds a new version itself and offers to install it. On desktop only builds carrying our signature are installed.

items.title: Nothing extra
items.text: No accounts inside the app, no ads, no in-app purchases. The subscription and the payment live in the bot.

items.q: Do I need Google Play or the App Store?
items.a: No. The file is downloaded from here, and the app finds new versions on its own.

items.q: How do I install it on a TV with no browser?
items.a: Use a downloader app such as Downloader: type sub.ndvsdom54.ru/tv.apk with the remote and the file starts immediately. The address is deliberately short and has no “https://”.

items.q: Why do banking and government sites usually break under a VPN?
items.a: Because their traffic goes through the tunnel and the site sees a foreign address. Here those sites stay on the direct route, and the rule list travels inside the app.

items.q: Can I use a key from another provider?
items.a: Yes, if it is a subscription link or a key in VLESS format. The app is the entrance to a tunnel; the server itself is not included.
Two at the same time. One subscription link covers the phone, the TV and the computer.

items.q: Is there a build for iPhone or Linux?
items.a: Not of our own. The subscription link works in third-party clients — v2RayTun on iPhone, or any client built on the sing-box core.
There are no accounts inside the app, no ads and no in-app purchases. For the subscription the bot knows only your Telegram account and the paid-until date.

last.lead: The file comes from here, and the trial starts inside the app itself — Telegram is not needed for that.

footer.note: The Android app is a fork of vpn4tv-native (GPL-3.0), the desktop app is open source (MIT), the sing-box core is GPL-3.0.
